title: Severe Bleeding
summary: Stop life-threatening bleeding: tourniquet, wound packing, or direct pressure.
sources: Stop the Bleed (American College of Surgeons)
TCCC Guidelines (Committee on Tactical Combat Casualty Care)
firstLine: Make sure the scene is safe. If you can reach 911 or anyone with medical training, send someone to call now. Put on gloves if you have them.

nodes.help: Yes if blood is spurting, pooling on the ground, soaking through clothing or bandages, a limb is partly or fully amputated, or the person is pale, confused, or fading.

options.label: No / not sure it is that bad

nodes.prompt: Where is the bleeding coming from?

nodes.help: A commercial tourniquet (CAT, SOF-T, SWAT-T) or a strap at least 1.5 inches wide plus a stick or rod to twist it tight.

nodes.title: Apply the tourniquet
steps: Place it 2 to 3 inches above the wound, between the wound and the heart. Never on a joint. If you can't find the wound quickly, put it as high on the limb as you can.
Pull the strap as tight as possible, then twist the rod until the bleeding stops.
Lock the rod in place.
Write the time on the tourniquet or the person's forehead.
If bleeding continues after it is tight, add a second tourniquet just above the first.
doNot: Do not loosen or remove the tourniquet once it is on. Leave that to medical care.
Do not use a thin cord, wire, or zip tie. It cuts tissue and does not stop arterial bleeding.
Do not cover the tourniquet. People need to see it.

nodes.title: Hard direct pressure
steps: Put cloth or gauze on the wound and press straight down with both hands, as hard as you can.
Lock your arms and use your body weight. Kneel on it if you must.
If the wound is deep, pack it with cloth first (push it into the wound until full), then press.
Keep pressing without peeking. Hold at least 10 minutes.
Meanwhile have someone improvise a tourniquet: a belt or wide strap plus a sturdy stick, twisted tight above the wound.
doNot: Do not lift your hands to check the wound. Releasing pressure restarts the bleeding.
Do not remove soaked cloth. Add more on top and keep pressing.

nodes.title: Pack the wound and press
steps: Find where the blood is coming from. Open clothing if needed.
Push gauze or clean cloth deep into the wound with your fingers, right onto the bleeding spot. Keep feeding it in until the wound is packed full.
Press down on the packed wound with both hands, hard.
Hold pressure for at least 3 minutes with hemostatic gauze, or 10 minutes with plain gauze or cloth.
Then wrap it tightly with a bandage to keep pressure on.
doNot: Do not put a tourniquet around the neck.
Do not remove packing once it is in. Add more on top if it soaks through.

nodes.title: Chest, belly, or back wound
steps: Press firmly on the wound with cloth or gauze.
Chest wound with bubbling or sucking sounds: cover it with plastic or a chest seal, taped on all sides (or three sides if that is all you can do).
Belly wound with organs showing: do not push them back in. Cover with a clean, moist cloth.
Let a conscious person with a chest wound sit up if that helps them breathe.
Get them to a surgeon as fast as possible. Torso bleeding cannot be fully controlled in the field.
doNot: Do not pack deep into the chest or belly.
Do not remove an object stuck in the body. Pad around it to keep it still.

nodes.prompt: Is it an arm or leg wound?

nodes.title: Escalate
steps: If a tourniquet is on: tighten it more, then add a second one right above it.
If no tourniquet: pack the wound and keep hard pressure. Keep trying to make a tourniquet.
Swap in a fresh person to hold pressure if your arms are giving out.

nodes.title: Repack and press harder
steps: Add more packing on top of what is already in the wound. Do not pull it out.
Press harder, with straight arms and your body weight.
Hold for another 10 minutes.
Swap in a fresh person to hold pressure if your arms are giving out.

nodes.title: Prevent shock
steps: Lay the person flat. Let them sit up only if they have a chest wound and breathe easier that way.
Keep them warm. Put insulation under them and cover them, even in mild weather. Cold makes bleeding worse.
Keep talking to them. Watch for confusion, pale or clammy skin, or fast breathing, which are signs of shock.
Check the wound and any tourniquet every few minutes for new bleeding.
doNot: Do not give food or drink if they may need surgery or are not fully alert.

nodes.title: Control the bleeding
steps: Press firmly on the wound with clean cloth or gauze for 10 minutes without lifting.
Once it stops, rinse the wound with clean water.
Cover with a clean bandage.
If bleeding soaks through or starts spurting, treat it as life-threatening.

nodes.title: Bleeding controlled - get them to care
steps: Get the person to a hospital or medic. Anyone who needed a tourniquet needs surgical care.
Keep them warm and lying down.
Recheck the wound and tourniquet every 5 minutes.
Tell the medic the tourniquet time and what you did. Use the handoff log below.

nodes.title: Get to a surgeon now
steps: Evacuate immediately by the fastest means available.
Keep pressure on the wound during transport.
Keep them warm. Watch their breathing.
If they stop breathing normally, start CPR.

nodes.title: Bleeding not controlled
steps: Keep hard pressure on the wound without stopping. Rotate people holding pressure.
Evacuate immediately by the fastest means available.
Keep them warm and lying flat.
If they stop breathing normally, start CPR.

nodes.title: Bleeding stopped
steps: Keep the wound clean and covered. Change the bandage daily or when wet.
Watch for infection over the next days: spreading redness, swelling, warmth, pus, red streaks, or fever.
Deep or gaping wounds, bites, and dirty wounds need medical care when it is available.
